implementation_notes: TypeScript adds types to the same shape: app.get('/users/:id', handler) registers the route, but Express's route string alone does not infer req.params; annotate Request<{ id: string }> yourself or use a typed router helper. The Action's inputs are then typed without a class, and the Responder is res.status(404).json(...) or a typed result the handler returns. Keep the domain behind an interface that never imports express types - that import is the signal the boundary leaked. The explicit responder module is justified when one handler must answer in several representations; otherwise a single typed handler is the idiomatic form.
pitfalls: Path parameters are strings: if the Domain expects a number or another value object, validate and convert at the Action; otherwise unchecked transport text reaches business logic.
Without an explicit DTO type as the response contract, a handler that returns a domain entity serialises internal fields.
Typing the handler parameter does not validate runtime input: malformed or missing parameters can still reach the Domain through casts or untyped routers -> validate at the boundary.

variants.name: NestJS controller with one route method
variants.idiom_name: NestJS single-route controller class with decorators
variants.implementation_notes: NestJS makes the Action a class: @Controller('users') plus @Get(':id') decorates a single handler method whose parameters are bound by decorators (@Param('id', ParseIntPipe)), and the Responder role is the returned DTO or a thrown HttpException - Nest serialises the return value and maps exceptions to statuses. A controller with one route method per class is the ADR shape; a controller with many methods drifts back to Page Controller. Choose NestJS when DI, validation pipes, guards and interceptors are wanted; choose the plain handler when the endpoint is one function.
pitfalls: Controllers are singletons: per-request state must live in a request-scoped provider, never in controller fields.
Throwing a plain Error yields a 500; only HttpException subclasses carry the intended status code and body.
Decorator metadata needs experimentalDecorators/emitDecoratorMetadata in tsconfig - a missing flag fails at runtime, not at compile time.
